scope: Six complete articles with related concepts and primary-source links. No standalone practices or graphics were requested.
examples: All contemporary named examples are illustrative fictional scenarios.
historical_approach: Ancient philosophical claims are distinguished from the narrower contemporary applications. No empirical efficacy claims are made.

visual_decisions.title: Negative Visualization
visual_decisions.reason: The distinction between anticipating a setback and rehearsing a response is explained through concrete examples; no graphic is needed for this article-only edition.

visual_decisions.title: Adversity as Training
visual_decisions.reason: The central issue is selecting an appropriate quality of conduct, which the contrasting interpersonal examples explain more precisely than a general training image.

visual_decisions.title: Dichotomy of Control
visual_decisions.reason: The action-versus-outcome distinction is developed across several cases; a binary diagram could obscure the treatment of influence and responsibility.

visual_decisions.title: Pause Before Assent
visual_decisions.reason: A linear diagram could imply a fixed psychological sequence; the examples better preserve the distinction between appearance, interpretation, and response.

visual_decisions.title: Voluntary Discomfort
visual_decisions.reason: The important qualifications concern what a limited experience can establish; a diagram would add little to the two contrasting examples.

visual_decisions.title: The View from Above
visual_decisions.reason: The changes of spatial and temporal scale are described directly; an illustration is optional and unnecessary for this article-only edition.
